name: Iowa
note: In Iowa, the funeral director who first takes custody of the body files the death certificate in the electronic death record system within three days of death and before final disposition. Every certifier, funeral director and county recorder must use that system. The attending physician, PA or ARNP certifies cause within 72 hours, or the medical examiner does so for nonnatural deaths. County recorders are the local registrars, and their death records are open to public inspection, although certified copies are restricted. The state registrar sends a quarterly decedent list to the state registrar of voters for cancellation, and may share data with child support services by automated exchange.

steps.title: Physician, PA or nurse pronounces death
steps.who: A physician or physician assistant, or a registered nurse or licensed practical nurse (who may pronounce an anticipated death in a hospital, care facility, Medicare-certified home health or hospice, assisted living or residential care facility, giving notice to a physician, ARNP or PA).
steps.summary: Iowa's definition of death rests on the announced opinion of a physician, PA, RN or LPN. Nurses may pronounce anticipated deaths in listed settings and must notify a physician, ARNP or PA.

steps.title: Deaths affecting the public interest reported to the medical examiner
steps.who: The physician in attendance, any law enforcement officer with knowledge, the funeral director or any other person present.
steps.trigger: A violent, unexpected, unexplained, custodial or otherwise listed death, or any nonnatural cause of death.
steps.summary: The county or state medical examiner must be told; it notifies law enforcement, takes charge of the body, investigates and reports to the state medical examiner and county attorney.

steps.title: Next of kin supplies personal data
steps.who: The next of kin or the best qualified person or source available.
steps.trigger: The funeral director first assuming custody of the body.
steps.summary: The funeral director obtains the personal data from the next of kin; the certificate includes the decedent's SSN if provided. Refusing to provide required information is a simple misdemeanour.

steps.title: Attending practitioner completes the medical certification
steps.who: The physician, physician assistant or advanced registered nurse practitioner in charge of the patient's care.
steps.trigger: Receipt of the death certificate from the funeral director (natural cause of death).

deadline.text: within 72 hours after receipt of the death certificate

steps.summary: For a natural death the attending practitioner signs the medical certification, attesting by signature or by an approved electronic process.

steps.title: Medical examiner certifies a nonnatural death
steps.who: The county or state medical examiner.
steps.trigger: A nonnatural cause of death, or an unexplained infant or child death.

deadline.text: within 72 hours after determination of the cause and manner of death

steps.summary: The medical examiner investigates cause and manner and signs the certification, or may defer to the attending practitioner where a pre-existing natural disease was the likely cause.

steps.title: Funeral director files the certificate in the electronic death record system
steps.who: The funeral director who first assumes custody of the body, or the person other than a funeral director who does so.

deadline.text: within three days after the death and before final disposition

steps.summary: The certificate is filed as the state registrar directs, through the electronic statewide vital records system that every certifier, funeral director and county recorder must use. It is registered by the county registrar (the county recorder) of the county of death.

steps.title: Burial-transit permit only after registration
steps.who: The county medical examiner, a funeral director or the state registrar issues the permit.
steps.trigger: Transfer out of state, or custody by someone other than a funeral director, medical examiner or EMS.
steps.summary: A permit cannot be issued until the completed, registered certificate is presented. Moving or disposing of a body without a required permit is a simple misdemeanour.

steps.title: Copy to the county of residence
steps.who: The state registrar, to the county registrar of the decedent's county of residence.
steps.trigger: A death outside the decedent's county of residence.
steps.summary: The state registrar sends a copy of the certificate and any amendments to the residence county, which records it; electronic access may replace the copy.

steps.title: Certified copies to entitled applicants
steps.who: The state registrar or any county registrar.
steps.trigger: A written, notarised application with ID and fee.
steps.summary: Certified copies go only to applicants showing a direct tangible interest and entitlement: the registrant's immediate family, legal representatives (including an attorney, executor, or the funeral director for one year), or others protecting a personal or property interest.

steps.title: Death records at the county are open to public inspection
steps.who: Any person, at the county registrar's office.
steps.trigger: A request under the public records law (chapter 22).
steps.summary: Non-fetal death records held by a county registrar may be inspected and copied as of right; county registrars give public-user access to the electronic system and issue uncertified copies.

steps.title: Quarterly list of decedents to the state registrar of voters
steps.who: The state registrar of vital statistics, to the state registrar of voters; then each county commissioner of elections.

deadline.text: once each calendar quarter; matching in the following month

steps.summary: A certified list of every reported decedent aged 17 or over is sent free each quarter. In the following month the commissioner runs the matching program and immediately cancels matched registrations.

steps.title: Death certificate data to child support services
steps.who: The state registrar and child support services (Iowa HHS).
steps.trigger: Agreement between the state registrar and child support services.
steps.summary: Any death-certificate information may be shared with child support services as mutually agreed, including by automated exchange.

steps.title: Confidential verification for government agencies
steps.who: The state registrar, for any federal, state, county or municipal agency, or other entity, acting in its official duties.
steps.summary: Agencies may get confidential verification of the facts in a death record, limited to official purposes; the state registrar may charge a negotiated fee.

steps.title: Data to the national division of vital statistics
steps.who: The state registrar, to the federal national vital statistics division.
steps.summary: The national division may receive copies or data for national statistics, for statistical use only unless the state registrar authorises otherwise.

steps.title: No list access for commercial firms; family presents certified copy
steps.trigger: Need to prove the death to a bank, insurer or other private body.
steps.summary: Rules deny entitlement to commercial firms seeking lists of events, names or addresses. Private bodies therefore rely on certified copies, which are prima facie evidence, or on the public county index.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: Three days after death and before final disposition.

informantDuty.note: The funeral director first taking custody files, or whoever else takes custody; next of kin supply data.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No independent review of all certificates; only nonnatural or listed deaths go to the medical examiner.

electronicRegistration.note: Statute requires every person with a death-certificate duty to participate in the electronic death record system, and the rule requires filing through it.

centralPopulationRegister.note: No population register; the state registrar keeps the vital records, and county recorders act as county registrars.

governmentPropagation.note: Under state law, registration reaches the residence county, the voter rolls (quarterly list) and, by agreement, child support services; other agencies may ask for verification. No statutory death feed to the DOT driver licence file or the Department of Revenue was found. Federal feeds such as SSA are in us-federal.

certificateAccess.note: Death records held by county registrars are open to inspection and copying as of right (uncertified). Certified copies are restricted to applicants with a direct tangible interest.

gaps: Administrative rules cited are 641 IAC chapters 95 and 97 as published in the IAC of 10 June 2026 (ARC 0142D/0144D, effective 1 July 2026). Earlier rule numbers have changed.

No statute or rule was found requiring vital records to notify the Iowa DOT (driver licences), the Department of Revenue or the Medicaid program of deaths. legis.iowa.gov full-text searches for decedent and death-certificate phrases with transportation, revenue or medical assistance returned no Code section.
A state electronic death registration feed to SSA (EDR) is not mentioned in Iowa statute or the chapters read; it belongs to the federal layer if sourced.
privateSectorVerification is deliberately left out of this file so that the us-federal value (LADMF/SSA) applies in the viewer. State rules exclude commercial list requests (641—95.8(2)(d)).
Probate notice to creditors (public stage) was not researched.
